sentences.en: Anyone who has had kids knows that they go through obsessive phases
sentences.zh: 任何养过孩子的人都知道，他们会经历各种痴迷阶段，

sentences.en: that can last anywhere from a few days to several years.
sentences.zh: 这些阶段可能持续几天，也可能长达数年。

sentences.en: I went through a lot of phases growing up.
sentences.zh: 我在成长过程中也经历过很多痴迷阶段。
说话的是制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: There was a brief train phase.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过短暂的火车迷时期。

sentences.en: Then, in preschool, I was obsessed with farming equipment.
sentences.zh: 后来在学前班时，我迷上了农用设备。

sentences.en: I could list obscure European tractor brands off the top of my head
sentences.zh: 我能随口列出那些冷门的欧洲拖拉机品牌，

sentences.en: like an old Italian wheat farmer.
sentences.zh: 就像个老练的意大利麦农一样。

sentences.en: But I think my most intense obsession, like many kids, was dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我最强烈的痴迷，和许多孩子一样，是恐龙。

sentences.en: I knew more about dinosaurs at the age of five than I do now.
sentences.zh: 五岁时我对恐龙的了解比现在还要多。

sentences.en: And I was all but certain that I would one day become a paleontologiSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我几乎确信自己将来会成为一名古生物学家。

sentences.en: I don't know exactly where this dinosaur obsession came from,
sentences.zh: 我不确定这种对恐龙的痴迷究竟从何而来，

sentences.en: but I think part of it was just that dinosaurs looked so cool.
sentences.zh: 但我认为部分原因仅仅是因为恐龙看起来太酷了。

sentences.en: I had all these books filled with incredible drawings of colorful dinosaurs
sentences.zh: 我当时有好多书，里面画满了色彩斑斓的恐龙，

sentences.en: leaping around, roaring, and tearing into one another.
sentences.zh: 它们跳跃、咆哮，互相撕咬。

sentences.en: I fell in love with the artwork in those books.
sentences.zh: 我爱上了那些书里的插画。

sentences.en: And at least for the time being, art is the only way we experience dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 至少在目前，艺术是我们体验恐龙的唯一方式。

sentences.en: We can study bones and fossils, but barring the invention of time travel
sentences.zh: 我们可以研究骨骼和化石，但除非发明了时间旅行，

sentences.en: or some Jurassic Park resurrection scenario,
sentences.zh: 或者出现某种《侏罗纪公园》式的复活场景，

sentences.en: we will never see these animals with our own eyes.
sentences.zh: 否则我们永远无法亲眼见到这些动物。

sentences.en: There are no photos or video, which means that if we want to picture how they look,
sentences.zh: 没有照片或视频，这意味着如果我们想想象它们的样子，
就必须有人把它们画出来。

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Dr. Robert Bakker, known to the folks in North Texas as Jurassic Bob.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是罗伯特·巴克博士，北德克萨斯州的人们称我为“侏罗纪鲍勃”。

sentences.en: Bob Bakker is one of the most famous living paleontologists,
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·巴克是当今最著名的古生物学家之一，

sentences.en: and he also happens to be a very skilled paleo artiSt.
sentences.zh: 同时他也是一位非常有造诣的古生物艺术家。

sentences.en: He thinks the two go hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 他认为这两者是相辅相成的。

sentences.en: Art is very important in teaching natural history science, maybe all science.
sentences.zh: 艺术在教授自然历史科学，甚至可能在所有科学教学中都非常重要。

sentences.en: Teach everyone art and everyone music, too.
sentences.zh: 教每个人艺术，也教每个人音乐。

sentences.en: When I interviewed him in a studio in Boulder, Colorado, he showed up an hour early,
sentences.zh: 当我在科罗拉多州博尔德市的一间工作室采访他时，他提前一小时就到了，

sentences.en: and he brought his own snacks.
He's got coffee and some apple pie.
sentences.zh: 他带了咖啡和一些苹果派。

sentences.en: This is so liberal, this place.
sentences.zh: 这地方真是太自由派了。

sentences.en: Once we got started with our interview, Bob said that, like me,
sentences.zh: 采访开始后，鲍勃说，像我一样，

sentences.en: he got obsessed with dinosaurs and dinosaur art pretty early on.
sentences.zh: 他很早就迷上了恐龙和恐龙艺术。

sentences.en: How I got hooked was a piece of journalism from 1953 Life magazine cover story called
sentences.zh: 我入坑是因为1953年《生活》杂志的一篇封面报道，标题叫

sentences.en: The World We Live In, and had pictures of dinosaurs and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 《我们生活的世界》，里面有恐龙之类的图片。

sentences.en: The cover image was the head of a long-necked dinosaur sitting in a swamp,
sentences.zh: 封面图是一只长颈恐龙的头，它坐在沼泽里，

sentences.en: munching on grass, with a stegosaurus in the background,
sentences.zh: 嚼着草，背景里有一只剑龙，

sentences.en: sort of staring off into space.
And inside was this long article about evolution.
sentences.zh: 里面还有一篇关于进化的长文。

sentences.en: After two hours with that Life magazine, I announced to my startled parents,
sentences.zh: 看完那本《生活》杂志两个小时后，我向我那吃惊的父母宣布：

sentences.en: Mom and Dad, I want to grow up and be a vertebrate paleontologiSt.
sentences.zh: “爸爸妈妈，我长大后想成为一名脊椎古生物学家。”
“这只是你成长过程中的一个阶段，很快就会过去的。”

sentences.en: But unlike me, dinosaurs weren't just the childhood phase for Jurassic Bob.
sentences.zh: 但与我不同的是，对于“侏罗纪鲍勃”来说，恐龙不仅仅是童年的痴迷。

sentences.en: By the time he headed off to college,
a career in vertebrate paleontology was still the game plan.
sentences.zh: 从事脊椎古生物学研究仍然是他的职业规划。

sentences.en: But it was kind of a strange time to be entering the field.
sentences.zh: 但那时进入这个领域有点奇怪。

sentences.en: In the mid-20th century, American dinosaur science was in a bit of a rut.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪中叶，美国的恐龙科学陷入了一点僵局。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs were considered big, dumb, cold-blooded reptiles.
sentences.zh: 恐龙被认为是笨重、愚蠢、冷血的爬行动物。
是注定要灭绝的进化失败者。

sentences.en: And that view of dinosaurs affected how they were painted and drawn.
sentences.zh: 这种对恐龙的看法影响了它们的绘画和描绘方式。

sentences.en: Most of the paintings of dinosaurs, they're not moving.
sentences.zh: 大多数恐龙画作中，它们都是静止的。

sentences.en: They're not interacting with each other.
There's no spark of intelligent social life.
sentences.zh: 没有智能社交生活的火花。

sentences.en: And their bodies were like hulking masses of flesh.
sentences.zh: 它们的身体就像一团团臃肿的肉块。

sentences.en: The way Brontosaurus and Diplodocus, the biggest dinosaurs, were illustrated,
sentences.zh: 雷龙和梁龙这些最大的恐龙，在插画中，

sentences.en: they were like giant, gray vacuum cleaners with very, very short legs.
sentences.zh: 就像巨大的灰色吸尘器，长着非常、非常短的腿。

sentences.en: And they were slowly pulling themselves across the landscape
sentences.zh: 它们在景观中缓慢地拖动着身体，

sentences.en: or sitting neck-deep in a fetid swamp.
sentences.zh: 或者坐在臭气熏天的沼泽里，没过脖子。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs were often drawn sitting in swamps, like on that Life magazine cover.
sentences.zh: 恐龙经常被画成坐在沼泽里，就像那本《生活》杂志的封面一样。

sentences.en: The thinking was they were so large, they couldn't possibly hold up their own body weight.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是它们太大了，不可能支撑起自己的体重。

sentences.en: And if they were drawn on land, they usually dragged their fat tails behind them as they walked.
sentences.zh: 如果它们被画在陆地上，走路时通常会拖着肥大的尾巴。

sentences.en: And that's where we were in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这就是20世纪60年代初我们的认知水平。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs were sad, cold-blooded dead ends in the history of life.
sentences.zh: 恐龙是生命史上可悲的、冷血的死胡同。

sentences.en: But paleontology was about to go through...

sentences.zh: 一场壮观且出人意料的彻底转变。

sentences.en: And a young Bob Bacher, just off to college, would find himself right in the thick of the action.
sentences.zh: 而刚上大学的年轻鲍勃·巴克，发现自己正处于这场变革的中心。

sentences.en: Freshman year, the Yale Geology Department took me, a bunch of other freshmen, out to Daig.
sentences.zh: 大一那年，耶鲁大学地质系带我和其他几名新生去了戴格。

sentences.en: The trip out west was led by one of Bob's professors at Yale, a paleontologist named John Ostrom.
sentences.zh: 这次西部之行由鲍勃在耶鲁的一位教授领导，他是一位名叫约翰·奥斯特罗姆的古生物学家。

sentences.en: And among other things, we dug up four raptors.
sentences.zh: 除其他发现外，我们还挖出了四只猛禽龙。

sentences.en: They were a new species of raptor that Professor Ostrom named Deinonychus.
sentences.zh: 它们是一个新的猛禽龙物种，奥斯特罗姆教授将其命名为恐爪龙。

sentences.en: And the bones were found really close together.
sentences.zh: 这些骨头被发现时靠得非常近。

sentences.en: But what really got Professor Ostrom excited was the anatomy of the skeleton.
sentences.zh: 但真正让奥斯特罗姆教授兴奋的是骨骼的解剖结构。

sentences.en: After studying the fossil remains back at Yale, Ostrom concluded that Deinonychus had not been a slow, plodding swamp creature.
sentences.zh: 在耶鲁研究了化石遗骸后，奥斯特罗姆得出结论：恐爪龙绝非缓慢、笨重的沼泽生物。

sentences.en: It had been fleet-footed, agile, and extremely active.
sentences.zh: 它曾是脚步轻快、敏捷且极其活跃的动物。

sentences.en: Ostrom began to argue that if you really looked at the anatomy of many dinosaurs, they looked less like lumbering lizards and more like super-athletic birds.
sentences.zh: 奥斯特罗姆开始论证，如果你仔细观察许多恐龙的解剖结构，它们看起来不像笨拙的蜥蜴，而更像超级运动型的鸟类。

sentences.en: And his student, Bob Bacher, found this idea really compelling.
sentences.zh: 而他的学生鲍勃·巴克觉得这个想法非常有说服力。

sentences.en: He remembers looking at a skeleton of a different dinosaur called Ornithelestes.
sentences.zh: 他记得曾看过一种叫鸟脚龙的恐龙骨架。

sentences.en: It really did look like a roadrunner with a long, bony tail and teeth.
sentences.zh: 它看起来确实像一只长着长骨尾和牙齿的走鹃。

sentences.en: But wow, it just spoke agility.
sentences.zh: 哇，它简直就是敏捷的代名词。

sentences.en: But then you read the textbooks and you're not supposed to believe that.
sentences.zh: 但当你读教科书时，你却被告知不该相信这一点。

sentences.en: As an undergraduate, Bacher dissected modern animals in an effort to better understand dinosaur musculature.
sentences.zh: 作为本科生，巴克解剖了现代动物，试图更好地理解恐龙的肌肉结构。

sentences.en: And he concluded that the old stereotypes about stupid, sluggish dinosaurs just didn't hold up.
sentences.zh: 他得出的结论是，关于恐龙愚蠢、迟钝的旧刻板印象根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: Now, this idea wasn't totally new.
sentences.zh: 其实，这个想法并非完全新鲜。

sentences.en: Bacher says that for decades, going back as early as the mid-19th century, there had been people saying that dinosaurs were smart, active, and bird-like.
sentences.zh: 巴克说，几十年来，早在19世纪中叶，就一直有人说恐龙聪明、活跃且像鸟类。

sentences.en: But these facts were forgotten about, really.
sentences.zh: 但这些事实实际上被遗忘了。
它们从教科书中消失了。

sentences.en: So Bacher decided to publish a paper in a Yale journal.
sentences.zh: 于是巴克决定在耶鲁的一本期刊上发表一篇论文。

sentences.en: I know what you should call this study.
sentences.zh: “我知道你应该给这项研究起什么名字。”

sentences.en: She said, you should call it the superiority of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 她说，你应该叫它《恐龙的优越性》。
它们不是进化的过时产物。

sentences.en: They weren't dead ends in the flow of Darwinian process.
sentences.zh: 它们不是达尔文进化过程中的死胡同。

sentences.en: They were top of the line.
But convincing people that dinosaurs were actually totally different than they had been depicted for the past 60 years
sentences.zh: 但是，要让人们相信恐龙实际上与过去60年所描绘的完全不同，

sentences.en: was going to require more than a few good academic papers to really change people's minds.
sentences.zh: 仅靠几篇优秀的学术论文是不够的，要真正改变人们的观念，

sentences.en: Sometimes you've got to show instead of tell.
sentences.zh: 有时你必须展示出来，而不是仅仅靠说。

sentences.en: And remember, Bacher was a skilled illustrator as well as a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，巴克不仅是一位科学家，还是一位熟练的插画家。

sentences.en: And so when John Ostrom wrote his definitive paper on Deinonychus, he asked Bacher to do the illustration.
sentences.zh: 所以当约翰·奥斯特罗姆撰写关于恐爪龙的权威论文时，他请巴克来做插图。

sentences.en: And I positioned the bones as if his raptor was running.
sentences.zh: 我把骨骼摆成了猛禽龙正在奔跑的样子。

sentences.en: In the picture, the raptor is nearly parallel with the ground.
sentences.zh: 在画中，猛禽龙几乎与地面平行。

sentences.en: Its left leg springing forward, its right leg curled tightly against its torso, preparing for the next stride.
sentences.zh: 它的左腿向前跃出，右腿紧紧蜷缩在躯干旁，为下一步跨步做准备。

sentences.en: The tail is high in the air.
It's beautiful and kind of terrifying.
sentences.zh: 它既美丽又有点令人恐惧。

sentences.en: Ostrom put the picture right on the front of his paper.
sentences.zh: 奥斯特罗姆把这张图放在了论文的首页。

sentences.en: And it quickly became an iconic drawing.
sentences.zh: 它很快成为了一幅标志性的画作。

sentences.en: No one had ever seen anything quite like it.
sentences.zh: 以前从没有人见过这样的东西。

sentences.en: This is Darren Naish, a paleontologist based in the UK.
sentences.zh: 这是达伦·奈什，一位常驻英国的古生物学家。

sentences.en: He's got like a flamboyant appearance.
He insists on wearing a cowboy hat all the time.
sentences.zh: 他坚持一直戴着牛仔帽。

sentences.en: He's got a giant bushy beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着巨大的浓密胡子。

sentences.en: And right from the late 60s, when he's, you know, starting to talk about this stuff,
sentences.zh: 从60年代末开始，当他开始谈论这些东西时，

sentences.en: he's drawing these agile, active dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 他就在画这些敏捷、活跃的恐龙。

sentences.en: Bacher finished up at Yale and went off to graduate school,
sentences.zh: 巴克在耶鲁毕业后去了研究生院，

sentences.en: where he continued to speak truth to the slow, dumb dinosaur establishment.
sentences.zh: 在那里他继续向那些认为恐龙缓慢、愚蠢的权威机构说真话。

sentences.en: He wrote academic and popular articles about how impressive dinosaurs had been.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了学术文章和科普文章，讲述恐龙曾经是多么令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: And he illustrated them all himself.
sentences.zh: 而且他亲自为它们绘制了插图。

sentences.en: He drew dinosaurs bounding across the prehistoric landscape like track and field stars
sentences.zh: 他画的恐龙像田径明星一样在史前景观中奔跑，
有着柔韧、肌肉发达的身体。

sentences.en: So prior, prior to this time, an animal like Tyrannosaurus would have been drawn as like
sentences.zh: 所以在此之前，像霸王龙这样的动物会被画成

sentences.en: a Godzilla type animal, dragging its tail on the ground.
sentences.zh: 哥斯拉那样的动物，在地上拖着尾巴。

sentences.en: It's not a particularly attractive beaSt.
sentences.zh: 那不是什么特别吸引人的野兽。

sentences.en: But under Bacher, you've got this thing shown with massive, bulging muscles.
sentences.zh: 但在巴克的笔下，这个东西展示出了巨大、隆起的肌肉。

sentences.en: And Bacher's athletic dinosaurs became a model for other paleo artists.
sentences.zh: 巴克笔下充满运动感的恐龙成为了其他古生物艺术家的典范。

sentences.en: So when my Deinonychus drawing appeared, some artists younger than I said,
sentences.zh: 所以当我的恐爪龙画作出现时，一些比我年轻的艺术家说：

sentences.en: huh, OK, now we can do it.
sentences.zh: “哈，好吧，现在我们可以这样画了。”

sentences.en: Artists like Gregory Paul embraced this new, exciting vision of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 像格雷戈里·保罗这样的艺术家拥抱了这种关于恐龙的全新、令人兴奋的愿景。

sentences.en: They started giving their dinosaurs vibrant colors and occasionally feathers
sentences.zh: 他们开始给恐龙涂上鲜艳的颜色，偶尔还会加上羽毛。
以真正强调它们的鸟类特征。

sentences.en: Soon, images of athletic, colorful dinosaurs were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 不久，充满活力、色彩斑斓的恐龙形象随处可见。

sentences.en: And they helped fuel the revolution that was taking place in paleontology.
sentences.zh: 它们推动了古生物学界正在发生的一场革命。

sentences.en: Throughout the 70s, more and more paleontologists got on board with Ostrom and Bacher's theories.
sentences.zh: 整个70年代，越来越多的古生物学家开始支持奥斯特罗姆和巴克的理论。

sentences.en: They found new fossils and footprint evidence suggesting that dinosaurs had been warm-blooded,
sentences.zh: 他们发现了新的化石和足迹证据，表明恐龙是温血动物，

sentences.en: This period has become known as the dinosaur renaissance,
sentences.zh: 这一时期被称为“恐龙文艺复兴”，

sentences.en: a moment when we totally rethought all of our assumptions about these incredible prehistoric animals.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我们彻底重新审视了关于这些神奇史前动物的所有假设。

sentences.en: And Darren Naish thinks art was a huge part of its success.
sentences.zh: 达伦·奈什认为艺术在这一成功中发挥了巨大作用。

sentences.en: I think that part of the reason that the dinosaurs of the dinosaur renaissance,
sentences.zh: 我认为“恐龙文艺复兴”时期的恐龙，

sentences.en: the dinosaurs of Ostrom and Bacher, drew in so many scientists in the 60s and 70s
sentences.zh: 也就是奥斯特罗姆和巴克笔下的恐龙，之所以在60和70年代吸引了那么多科学家，

sentences.en: was because it was accompanied by brilliant visuals.
sentences.zh: 是因为它们伴随着精彩的视觉呈现。

sentences.en: If anyone missed out on this scientific revolution
sentences.zh: 如果有人错过了这场科学革命，

sentences.en: and still thought that dinosaurs were slow and stupid,
sentences.zh: 还认为恐龙是缓慢而愚蠢的，
那么这种想法在1993年终结了。

sentences.en: The dinosaurs in Jurassic Park are very active.
sentences.zh: 《侏罗纪公园》里的恐龙非常活跃。
它们就是“恐龙文艺复兴”的化身。

sentences.en: And when that movie came out,
the whole world got to see these fierce athletic creatures
sentences.zh: 全世界都看到了这些凶猛、矫健的生物，

sentences.en: running through kitchens and eating lawyers off of toilets.
sentences.zh: 它们在厨房里奔跑，把律师从马桶上叼走。

sentences.en: And once you've seen the dinosaurs in Jurassic Park,
sentences.zh: 一旦你看过《侏罗纪公园》里的恐龙，
你就再也无法抹去那种印象了。

sentences.en: I think it cemented the notion of athletic dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 我认为它巩固了“矫健恐龙”的概念。

sentences.en: He draws dinosaurs for a living.
I'm a paleo artist, which means that I draw and paint prehistoric animals.
sentences.zh: 我是一名古生物艺术家，这意味着我绘制和描绘史前动物。

sentences.en: Conway got interested in paleo art after reading Bob Bacher's book,
sentences.zh: 康威在读了鲍勃·巴克的书《恐龙异端》后，对古生物艺术产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: And in the early part of his career,
he drew dinosaurs that looked a lot like Bacher's,
sentences.zh: 他画的恐龙看起来和巴克画的非常像，
